proof_reading.audit: Finite second moments establish integrability; positive-definite Gram gives the unique loss minimizer by the cross-term identity. The sample full-rank projection is distinguished from random-design population orthogonality. Partial regression is derived by minimizing over nuisance coordinates, and its residualized Gram rank is proved. Orthogonality is explicitly zero cross moments; zero covariance additionally follows when an intercept centers residuals. Correlation with constants is undefined.

Conditional mean zero, full column rank and known positive-definite covariance are explicit. Whitening uses the prior spectral square root. For every linear unbiased comparator AX=I, D=A-A_G has DX=0 and DΣA_G′=0; the covariance difference is DΣD′. Contrast equality uses positive definiteness. Reversed precision weights supply a concrete failure under a wrong covariance.

Only conditional spherical Gaussian errors with σ²>0,n>p are used. Orthogonal coordinates split fitted and residual directions; the restriction-normalizing matrix has orthonormal rows, extended to a full orthogonal basis. Density invariance supplies independence, chi-square residual degrees of freedom and exact t/F. Non-Gaussian two-sign finite coverage is only 1/2 despite homoskedasticity.

Fixed p, iid (x,y), positive-definite Q and E[(norm(x)+abs(y))^4]<infinity. Each needed fourth-degree mixed moment is explicitly dominated. Exact score expansion plus finite-second-moment CLT gives root-n order; residual meat replacement bounded by 2||δ|| P||x||^3|e|+||δ||² P||x||^4. Contrast studentization requires positive limiting variance; negligible singular/nonpositive-variance events are handled. Singular sample Gram estimates receive an explicit zero convention solely to define the limit sequence; operational reports flag rank failure.

Projection bounds 0≤h≤1, trace p; max h bounded by ||Q_n^-1|| sqrt(sum||x||^4)/n tends to zero. Uniform multiplier differences prove the same asymptotic limit for HC2/3. HC2 conditional expectation rationale is scoped to spherical covariance. Singleton indicator example has leverage one and explicit undefined HC2/3. Undefined HC2/HC3 samples are explicitly assigned zero solely for the asymptotic sequence, with their probability shown negligible.

Fixed finite categories with positive probabilities and positive finite conditional variances; conditional mean zero centers each group score. Group residual-variance estimates converge by ratio LLN and explicit residual replacement; absent/zero-variance groups use the declared asymptotically negligible fallback. Weight errors times normalized centered group scores vanish without independence of the estimates. Weighted Gram and squared-weight meat are both controlled. Mean misspecification can change the target and defeat oracle equivalence.

IID whole clusters, bounded sizes, whole-cluster fourth moments and positive-definite per-cluster Gram. Target is pooled loss per cluster, not equally weighted cluster means. Cluster score sums are centered, their LLN/CLT uses sqrt(G), and the residual replacement bound uses A_g,B_g and finite second products. CR0 is Vhat/G. Fixed G, growing/dominant clusters and dependence across clusters are excluded.

Two-sided strictly stationary fixed-m dependence is defined by independence of separated past/future sigma-fields, not mere zero covariances. Bounded coordinates imply bounded centered scores. Covariance counting gives LLN and long-run covariance. Blocks of floor(n^(1/3)) separated by m are mutually independent; omitted count O(nm/ell+ell+m), omitted variance O(count), and normalized omission L2 vanishes. Retained variance shares the full limit by Cauchy-Schwarz. Third-order smooth Gaussian replacements sum to zero via deterministic b_n=B ell_n/sqrt(n) and max variance; explicit C3 monotone transitions establish CDF convergence. Degenerate contrasts use L2. Only inherited Cramer-Wold characterization is invoked for vector notation.

Exact zero-extension windows include all edge multiplicities L+1 and L+1-lag. Each quadratic form is a sum of squares. For consistency, true lag-product estimates have variance O((m+lag+1)/n); summed mean deviations are O((L+1)sqrt((m+L+1)/n)). Finite-range bias is O(1/(L+1)+1/n); fitted-score replacement is O_P((L+1)/sqrt(n)). L→infinity and L^3/n→0 are conservative sufficient rates. Fixed L retains attenuation and is not called consistent for nonzero lag covariance.

Projection is distinct from structural causality, exact covariance from estimated covariance and finite laws from asymptotic approximations. Weighting can change estimands. No uniform weak-rank/high-dimensional, arbitrary dependent, general FGLS, few-cluster exact or post-selection theorem is asserted.
